uncited: Image-Driven Non-Photorealistic Scene Editing (NPSE) stylizes volume visualization scenes by transferring the artistic style of a reference image onto a 3D Gaussian representation, ensuring multi-view consistency.

It distinguishes itself from sibling methods like [StyleSplat](11108-text-driven-non-photorealistic-scene-editing.md) by embedding texture attributes within Gaussian primitives, allowing each primitive to express multiple colors and reducing elliptical artifacts, while leveraging a combined NNFM and CLIP loss strategy to capture both local and global style patterns.
*   A set of multi-view input images of the scene.
*   Text prompts (optional, used for classifier-free guidance in the IP2P model).
*   A set of textured Gaussian primitives representing the stylized scene.
*   **Gaussian Primitive:** Defined by position, covariance, opacity, base color, and a **texture attribute**.
The texture attribute allows the primitive to store multiple color values, enabling complex style expression.
**Initialization:** Initialize Gaussian primitives from the input multi-view images.
**Optimization:** Optimize the Gaussian parameters (position, covariance, opacity, base color, and texture attributes) to match the reference style.
*   **Neural Style Loss (NNFM):** To preserve detailed style patterns and ensure multi-view consistency.
**Rendering:** Render the scene using the optimized textured Gaussian primitives.
Captures local and global style patterns.
*   Use when high-quality, multi-color stylization with multi-view consistency is needed, and storage/compute for optimization is available.
*   Avoid if minimal model size or fastest rendering speed is the primary constraint (use StyleSplat instead).
It builds upon the Gaussian Splatting technique and extends it with texture attributes for non-photorealistic rendering in volume visualization contexts.
The method addresses the limitations of single-color Gaussian primitives in capturing complex artistic styles.
